newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index eases 0.2 pts in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index eases 0.2 pts in listless trade.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Friday, with the SAX index easing 0.20 points to 193.55.
Overall turnover rose sharply to 828.81 million crowns, from 31.61 million, due to several off-floor deals involving large packages of bank VUB.

But only 850 and 449 shares were traded on the BSE listed and unlisted floors respectively, and brokers said the current stagnation, resulting from economic and political instability in the country, continued.
"There is nothing new to say," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said. "Some shares closed higher, but traded insignificant volumes," he added.
Steel maker VSZ traded 287 shares to close up 20 crowns at 700, but Betko said the higher price was only a single-share correction at the end of the bourse's session.
One package of 160,000 and two other packages -- both of 81,000 shares -- were traded in VUB bank directly at prices of 1,700 to 1,880 crowns, against 1,550 crowns on the floor.
"This is a long-lasting story in VUB," Betko said.

"Effectively, it is an indirect privatisation, as several VUB shareholders are strenghtening their positions this way. In fact, it hasn't much to do with trading on BSE, it's only registered there," he added.
